summary: This memo gives a brief overview of the Standing Documents series from the North American Directory Forum, which dealt with running X.500 directory services in North America. It is informational and was replaced by RFC 1758.

plainLanguage.summary: The North American Directory Forum brought competing service providers together to plan a shared X.500 public directory. RFC 1417 summarizes the documents they wrote to coordinate its structure, operation, and policies; RFC 1758 later replaced this overview.

subtitle: A guide to the North American Directory Forum's cooperative directory documents.

tldr.problem: Competing providers planned to offer a shared public directory service in North America using X.500, so they needed agreements for operating it cooperatively.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 1417 summarizes the NADF Standing Documents, which cover the service, its directory structure, naming, security, privacy, and administration.
tldr.outcome: RFC 1417 was obsoleted by RFC 1758 and is a historical overview of the NADF document series.

today: RFC 1417 is Informational and was obsoleted by RFC 1758.

sections.title: Why the NADF Wrote Standing Documents
sections.content:
The North American Directory Forum (NADF) was a collection of service providers planning to offer a cooperative Public Directory Service in North America using the CCITT X.500 Recommendations. The challenge was to create one cooperative service even though its providers competed with one another.

RFC 1417 is an informational overview of the NADF Standing Document series. The memo says that it does not specify an Internet standard.
sections.plainLanguage: Competing providers wanted to run one shared public directory. The NADF documents set out agreements to help them work together.

sections.title: What the Document Series Covers
sections.content:
The numbered series runs from SD-0, this overview, through SD-12. SD-1 defines the NADF's scope, and SD-2 describes issues of interest. Other documents cover service agreements, the directory schema, the pilot, and security and privacy policy and mechanisms.

SD-5 describes the national directory tree and naming scheme for Canada and the United States. It separates a public name space for publicly recognized entities from private name spaces managed by individual providers. SD-7 explains links between those spaces, and SD-9 describes how the Central Administration for NADF coordinates and distributes the shared information.
sections.plainLanguage: Each document handles part of the work, such as what the directory contains, how names are organized, and how providers share links between their directories.

sections.title: Availability and Status
sections.content: At the time of writing, the Standing Documents were available only in hardcopy and PostScript, not ASCII. The memo lists postal mail, anonymous FTP, and an email archive server as ways to obtain them. It states that security issues are not discussed in this memo.
sections.plainLanguage: The series was distributed as printed documents and PostScript files. RFC 1417 explained how readers at the time could request copies.
